context: Kenji finishes a long art project; reflects with Ren.
purpose: Two artists in quiet end-of-project reflection.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.style: Soft exhale of relief on the opening. Warm, tired contentment underneath. Slow pace, like settling into a chair. Slight Kansai drawl softening the edges.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.en: Thank you for your hard work.
lines.style: Quiet, genuine respect. No performative politeness — just steady acknowledgment. Soft attack, gentle trailing. The voice of someone who notices what was done.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 先週、たった一枚やのに、ようけ時間。
lines.en: Last week it was just one piece, but it took so much time.
lines.style: Reflective, almost talking to himself. Warm Kansai lilt on the vowels. Not complaining — observing. A small chuckle of recognition in the delivery.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 前作と比、どう感じます?
lines.en: How does it compare to your last work?
lines.style: Genuine curiosity, not testing. Soft, engaged. Leans forward slightly in the voice. Wants to understand what he's thinking.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 同じくらいの満足感、ある。
lines.en: I feel just as satisfied with this one.
lines.style: Warm and certain. A slight nod in the voice. Content without needing to elaborate. Kansai softness framing quiet pride.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 後ろ、見ても、誇れる仕事や。
lines.en: Looking back at it, it's work you can be proud of.
lines.style: Steady conviction delivered gently. Not flattery — statement of fact. Warm respect. The voice of someone who means what he says and doesn't need to say it twice.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 反省、ようけあるけど、進む。
lines.en: I have a lot of things I'd reflect on, but we move forward.
lines.style: Philosophical and accepting. Warm Kansai drawl. Acknowledgment without weight — aware of what could improve, unbothered by the weight of it. Gentle trailing on 「進む」.
